correctness.rationale: At a cubic vertex the three face angles exhaust the three unordered incident pairs. Conversely a complete angle cover glues disks with every edge incident twice and with a single circular vertex link at every vertex; the orientability constraints and Euler characteristic 14−21+7=0 identify the torus. The classification and flip counts were independently reproduced using rotations, not the frozen angle-cover programs. In an oriented cellular embedding the local cyclic orders determine face walks up to coherent choice of orientation; there are exactly two orders at each cubic vertex. Tracing every one of the 2^14 systems gave 16 orientations with seven distinct simple length-six faces, yielding eight boundary sets, twice each under reversal. Exhausting the 24 incidence bijections and toggling their alternating faces gave three 7-cycles and three isolated matchings for each set, with exactly one edge of each face label in each cycle. The frozen triples partition all matchings and exhaust all eight edge-disjoint triples. Exactly 28 six-cycles and 84 individual flips were found; each occurs twice across the eight systems. Removing any face label breaks every 7-cycle; retaining s labels gives exactly 3s edges and hence 24−3s components in a forest. The independent replay also checked all 127 proper subsets per system. Replay with python3 /workspace/branches/448c5fd8-2195-4b24-a20c-34156db20879/heawood_rotation_replay.py; the companion .out contains the incidence and label records. Supplied certificate and verifiers were inspected without executing the frozen code. No claim about embeddings with nonsimple faces is needed.

evidence: Tratnik–Ye prove bipartiteness and induced-hypercube representation subject to a proper even-face subset and give a separate full-face counterexample. Liang–Zhang prove that nontrivial perfect matchings in a fixed toroidal polyhex are in the same component iff their two cut flows agree and give a formula for the number of trivial matchings. Shiu–Lam–Zhang study existence of simultaneous alternating disjoint faces rather than transitions of every individual matching.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The general results apply to reconfiguration or resonance for a specified embedded graph; they do not enumerate all possible hexagonal boundary sets on a labeled Heawood graph or assign their frozen triples. Proper-subset bipartiteness or hypercube embedding alone does not force the exact forest/component counts. The unavailable 2008 text is documented as a risk, not a finding of absence.

value.rationale: The choice of admissible torus faces changes the allowed moves on the same finite matching space. A complete census of that natural variation, including the exact embedding-to-factorization correspondence and how individual hexagon flips distribute among embeddings, separates geometry-dependent freezing from the known unrestricted trade graph. A user of this standard small toroidal example can determine exactly which embeddings freeze a matching or allow a given trade. This is more than a one-map repeat or a matching-count recomputation.
